predictions.quote: I think the revenue scale will continue for like the next 2 or 3 years probably for Nvidia.
predictions.prediction: Nvidia's revenue will continue to grow at large scale (i.e., remain at or above its early-2024 run-rate and not materially contract) for approximately the next 2–3 years from February 2024.

predictions.quote: The Wall Street analysts I've been listening to think that in five years they're still going to have 60 something percent market share, so they're going to have a substantial percentage of this market or this Tam.
predictions.prediction: Consensus Wall Street analyst expectations as of February 2024 are that Nvidia will still hold roughly "60-something percent" of the GPU market used for AI workloads five years later (around 2029).

predictions.quote: I mean, we're just at the beginning of a wave that's probably going to last at least a decade.
predictions.prediction: The AI-driven wave of new applications (both consumer and enterprise) powered by cloud data centers and GPUs will continue to expand for at least the next decade from 2024, i.e., through at least 2034.

predictions.quote: there's a lot of market cap for grok to gain by just being able to produce these things at scale.
predictions.prediction: If Groq ("grok with a Q") is able to produce its LPU chips at scale, its market capitalization will increase substantially from its early-2024 level of roughly "a billion something" (i.e., it will become worth significantly more than a low-single-digit billion dollars over the following years).

predictions.quote: Now, I think what's going to happen now is in light of this, the reaction to the rollout is, do I think they're going to get rid of bias? No, they're going to make it more subtle... I think they're simply going to they're going to dial down the bias to be less obvious.
predictions.prediction: Following the public backlash to Gemini’s rollout (Feb 2024), Google will not remove ideological bias from the model but will instead adjust it to be less obvious and more subtle, rather than changing the underlying values or objectives.

predictions.quote: I think the only way that a company like Google or others that are trying to create a general purpose, knowledge Q&A type service are going to be successful is if they enable some degree of personalization... If they don't allow this, eventually everyone will come across some search result or some output that they will say doesn't meet their objectives... they're going to say, I don't want to use this product anymore.
predictions.prediction: General-purpose AI Q&A services (such as Google Gemini) will only be commercially successful if they implement user-level personalization of values and filtering; if they do not, over time a significant share of users will abandon these products after encountering outputs that conflict with their objectives.

predictions.quote: And so it is actually an opportunity for many models to proliferate, for open source, to win.
predictions.prediction: Due to dissatisfaction with heavily filtered/bias-tuned large models, multiple competing AI models will proliferate and open‑source models will gain a significant competitive advantage ('win') in the market over more tightly controlled proprietary models.

predictions.quote: what I'm afraid of is that what Google will do is not change the underlying ideology that this AI model has been trained with, but rather they'll dial it down to the point where they're harder to call out. And so the energy will just be more subtle.
predictions.prediction: In response to criticism of Gemini, Google will not materially change the ideological framing of the model but will instead make the biased behaviors less overt and harder to detect, rather than eliminating them.

predictions.quote: We are going to be the truth tellers in this new world of AI. So when everybody else hallucinates, you can trust Google. To tell you the truth, that is a $10 trillion company, right?
predictions.prediction: If Google were to massively license high‑quality training data (on the order of tens of billions of dollars per year) and position itself as the most reliable, truth‑focused AI provider, this strategy could support Google achieving a market valuation on the order of $10 trillion in the future.

predictions.quote: I think we're like in the 1996 era of Llms, and in a couple of months, the pace, things are changing. predictions.prediction: Within a few months after February 2024, the quality of LLMs will improve so quickly that people will look back on early‑2024 LLM behavior (and this discussion) as primitive and notably bad, analogous to how 1996 web search compares to later eras.

predictions.quote: I actually think to your point, Google could be going down the wrong path here in a way that they will lose users and lose consumers, and someone else will be there eagerly to sweep up with a better product. I don't think that the market is going to fail us on this one
predictions.prediction: If Google continues on its current Gemini/product-ideology path, it will lose a meaningful number of users/consumers to competing AI/search products that offer a better experience; competitive market forces will correct for Google’s missteps rather than allowing it to retain dominance with an inferior product.

predictions.quote: I think the open internet has enough data that there isn't going to be a monopoly on information by someone spending money for content from third parties. I think that there's enough in the open internet to give our all. Give us all kind of, you know, the security that we're not going to be monopolized away into some disinformation age.
predictions.prediction: No single company will be able to achieve a monopoly on training data or information control for AI models through paid content licensing, because the open internet already contains sufficient data to prevent effective monopolization and a resulting 'disinformation age' driven by one actor.
